ko.executive_summary: HPC and datacenter ecosystem showing significant R&D infrastructure expansion: Samsung Heavy Industries expanding Busan R&D center following U.S. FLNG contract win, Nvidia establishing Shanghai R&D presence, and talent competition intensifying with SK hynix removing degree requirements. Infrastructure stress also evident as Tesla Dojo supercomputer reportedly caused power grid disruption in Palo Alto. Intel aggressively recruiting foundry executives to compete with TSMC and Samsung.

Nvidia opening Shanghai R&D center
TSE establishing Semiconductor Test Design Center in Daegu
SK hynix dropping degree requirements for AI hiring
Tesla Dojo supercomputer caused power grid trip in Palo Alto
Intel recruiting executives from competing foundries

implications.text: South Korean (Busan, Daegu) and Chinese (Shanghai) R&D center investments signal intensified regional AI infrastructure competition
SK hynix removing credential barriers demonstrates extreme competition for AI engineering talent in HPC space
Intel's executive recruitment from TSMC and Samsung indicates preparation for aggressive foundry market repositioning
Tesla Dojo power grid incident highlights emerging power delivery challenges for hyperscale AI computing infrastructure

ko.counterpoint: Palo Alto grid incident is isolated event; industrial power infrastructure typically handles supercomputer loads with proper planning.
